title: Hydraulic Envelope and Representation Geometry Qualification
objective: Determine whether the qualified F-LMFP08 homogeneous-face representation can be extended to a materially broader hydraulic envelope with a coordinate system regular through h=0, fail-closed boundaries, bounded table cardinality and qualified heterogeneous-interface continuity, without changing production code or weakening mass and reference gates.

staged_gates.A_coordinate_and_envelope: select and qualify a monotone head coordinate regular at h=0 with near-saturated and dry-tail coverage
staged_gates.B_homogeneous_face_matrix: rerun F-LMFP08 identities and Darcian face-oracle matrix over expanded materials and face lengths
staged_gates.C_heterogeneous_interface: qualify equal-flux interface continuity, accuracy and bounded local solve behaviour over material contrasts
staged_gates.D_cardinality_and_cost: measure material/geometry-class counts, table memory and preparation/runtime cost proxies
staged_gates.E_transient_regression: rerun F-LMFP07/F-LMFP08 ordinary and strong-gradient transient gates with exact mass conservation

candidate_questions: Can a signed/asinh-like or piecewise linear-log pressure-head coordinate remove the h=0 singularity without degrading dry-tail resolution?
Can saturated and near-saturated face behaviour be represented without a special discontinuous branch?
How dry can the table extend before interpolation density or constitutive dynamic range becomes impractical?
Can the homogeneous correction be reused across a bounded set of face-length classes or normalized to reduce geometry cardinality?
Does the heterogeneous equal-flux interface remain continuous and accurate when either half-face crosses the near-saturated region?
What envelope boundary should fail closed rather than extrapolate?
